title: INSTEAD OF Trigger on a View
description: Create an INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger on a view to direct inserts to the underlying table.

data.text: You have a view `ActiveEmployees` that selects only current employees. Write an INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger so that inserting into the view automatically routes the data into the `Employees` table.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- Create the view
CREATE VIEW ActiveEmployees
AS
SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName, Department, Salary, HireDate
FROM Employees
WHERE IsActive = 1;
GO

-- Create INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger
CREATE TRIGGER trg_InsteadOfInsert_ActiveEmployees
ON ActiveEmployees
INSTEAD OF INSERT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    INSERT INTO Employees (FirstName, LastName, Department, Salary, HireDate, IsActive)
    SELECT
        FirstName,
        LastName,
        Department,
        Salary,
        ISNULL(HireDate, GETDATE()),
        1 -- Always insert as active
    FROM inserted;
END;
GO

-- Usage:
-- INSERT INTO ActiveEmployees (FirstName, LastName, Department, Salary)
-- VALUES ('Alice', 'Smith', 'Engineering', 95000);

data.title: Explanation
data.text: INSTEAD OF triggers fire INSTEAD OF the original DML action — the INSERT never reaches the view directly; the trigger handles it entirely. They are commonly used on views to make them updatable, especially for complex views involving joins. The `inserted` pseudo-table contains the rows being inserted.
